title: Microscopic equivalence of the vortex-entry current and the depairing current in a superconducting thin-film strip
abstract: The current at which vortices enter a superconducting strip is usually identified in Pearl--London theory with the disappearance of an edge barrier. This work reformulates the same question microscopically as the loss of local stability of the vortex-free current-carrying state, using the fixed-current Gibbs functional of dirty-limit Usadel theory, which is valid at arbitrary temperatures. For an ideal homogeneous thin-film strip at zero applied field, with self-field effects neglected, the stability of the vortex-free state is examined against both spatially uniform and nonuniform perturbations. The barrier-disappearance current is shown to be set by the uniform perturbation and to coincide exactly with the depairing current.
summary: This theoretical paper microscopically investigates the critical current for vortex entry in a superconducting thin film strip. By analyzing the stability of the zero-vortex state using advanced Usadel theory, the authors demonstrate that this threshold current precisely matches the depairing current under ideal conditions. This provides a rigorous, microscopic confirmation of established superconducting critical current concepts.
main_problem: The work aims to microscopically determine the current density at which magnetic vortices enter a superconducting thin-film strip ($J_v$) and compare this value against the depairing current ($J_{dp}$).
main_result: For an ideal homogeneous zero-field strip, the microscopic stability analysis shows that the vortex-entry current is exactly equal to the depairing current ($J_v = J_{dp}$).
method: The problem is formulated by analyzing the stability of the vortex-free state using the fixed-current Gibbs functional derived from dirty-limit Usadel theory, examining both uniform and nonuniform perturbations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a homogeneous superconducting thin-film strip assumed to be infinite in one direction and analyzed at zero applied magnetic field. The theoretical framework relies on the fixed-current Gibbs functional of dirty-limit Usadel theory.
key_observables: Vortex-entry current density ($J_v$), depairing current density ($J_{dp}$), and the stability criterion derived from minimizing the quadratic energy cost ($\delta^2 G$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$) relative to $T_c$, applied current density ($J$), and dimensionless parameters related to gauge-invariant momentum ($Q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an ideal, homogeneous strip geometry and neglects magnetic self-field effects for the primary calculation.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by reformulating the vortex entry problem as a local stability analysis of the current-carrying state. It first examines uniform perturbations to find a candidate critical current, and then rigorously proves that nonuniform modes do not destabilize the system at lower currents than the uniform mode.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous application of stability analysis (saddle-node bifurcation) using functional methods is relevant to understanding phase transitions or instability thresholds in complex quantum systems beyond standard BCS theory.
